comparisons.peer_summary: The Company uses the acquisition method of accounting for business combinations, allocating purchase consideration to assets and liabilities based on fair value as of the acquisition date, with any excess recorded as goodwill.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose their specific methodology for determining fair value in the context of business combinations and asset valuation, though they address different asset classes. AVGO specifies the 'multi-period excess earnings method' for valuing In-Process Research and Development (IPR&D), while AMD discloses the general application of the acquisition method to allocate purchase consideration to assets and liabilities at fair value. Both disclosures are rooted in the income approach logic of estimating future cash flows or fair values at acquisition, but AVGO provides a specific technical model for a specific intangible asset, whereas AMD provides a general policy statement for business combinations.

sentences.text: The fair value of IPR&D was determined using the multi-period excess earnings method under the income approach.
This method reflects the present value of the projected cash flows that are expected to be generated by the IPR&D, less charges representing the contribution of other assets to those cash flows.

The acquisition method of accounting requires the Company to allocate the purchase consideration to the assets acquired and liabilities assumed from the acquiree based on their respective fair values as of the acquisition date.
